To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

{\em entangled spin-orbit states} of the electron wave functions are responsible for the spin-polarization of the current and that the spin coherence of the injected electrons is determined by their {\em entanglements} with the orbital degrees of freedom of the disordered Rashba conductor.

{\em The spin-resolved Landauer transmission matrix yields the reduced spin state of an injected spin-polarized electron which is a quantum state that encodes the spin-orbit entanglement of its spin and its orbital degrees of freedom, and the quantum information measures of entanglements of the electron spin and its orbital states provide a complete characterization of the detected spin-polarization of a transmitted electron.}
the spin and orbital degrees-of-freedom of an electron are entangled in the presence of spin-orbit coupling and that the entangled state can be detected in a quantum coherent spintronic device.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the quantum theory of electron spin transport in spin-polarized quantum-coherent structures, which are of interest for future spintronic devices.

the development of a theoretical framework for a quantitative description of quantum transport of spin-polarization in mesoscopic spintronic devices, with particular attention to the effects of electron spin-orbit coupling on spin-polarized electron transport and spin-coherence in semiconductor spintronic nanostructures.
a fundamental question: {\em how to use quantum entanglement of the spin and orbital degrees-of-freedom of a single particle to control quantum transport in mesoscopic spintronic devices?}
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in spintronics, quantum entanglement of electron spin and orbital degrees is an essential ingredient of the quantum transport phenomena.
{\em quantum entanglement of spin and orbital degrees-of-freedom is the origin of spin-coherence in spintronic devices}.

the Landauer-B\"uttiker theory, when applied to a spintronic structure, provides the spin-resolved transmission matrix which, in the present case, is used not only to calculate the conductance but to extract also the spin density operator, thereby allowing us to evaluate the entanglement of spin and orbital states in spintronic transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the entanglement of the spin and orbital degrees-of-freedom is a {\em resource} for the spin-polarization of the transmitted current and the spin-coherence of the spin-polarized current, which are the key ingredients of spintronics and spin-polarized transport.

the quantum transport theory of entanglement of the spin and orbital degrees-of-freedom in the spintronic structures provides a novel tool for the design of the semiconductor spintronic quantum devices.
the entangled spin-orbital states are a natural consequence of the spin-orbit interaction and, in particular, the Rashba effect in the presence of charge scattering.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the entanglement of spin and orbital states in spintronic structures is an intrinsic quantum-mechanical property which is {\em not} a result of a particular measurement procedure, but rather is a consequence of the quantum-mechanical description of a mesoscopic system.

the entanglement of electron spin and orbital degrees-of-freedom, in the presence and absence of spin-orbit coupling and spin-dependent charge scattering, can be {\em detected} in spin-resolved quantum transport measurements.
the spin-polarization of the transmitted electron is a {\em non-classical} quantum-mechanical quantity which is not a simple average over a classical probability distribution of spin states.
